title: Activepieces Community Edition vs Enterprise: 2026 Pricing
summary: Activepieces Community Edition vs Enterprise compares free self-hosted software to paid plans with SSO and vendor support. Determine which fits your needs.
body_markdown:
## How Activepieces quotes enterprise and Embed


Before a number appears, four inputs go into a sales quote. They're how many people use the platform, how many credits they consume, whether it runs in the vendor's cloud or on your own infrastructure, and what level of support you need.


The number of flows you build isn't an input.


Activepieces' public pricing page lists unlimited flows on every plan from Free through Ultimate, and the only meter is credits: a run is 1 credit however many steps it has, so splitting one fragile mega-automation into ten small, maintainable flows leaves the quote where it was.


Zapier's pricing page counts a task for every action and Make's counts a credit for every module, so on those the tidier design costs more each time it runs. MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


### What drives Enterprise edition pricing quotes


Users and credits are the volume lines. More named users means more seats to administer, and more monthly credits means more executions to run on your behalf.


It is deployment model that buyers underestimate most. A cloud contract means the vendor operates the environment. A self-hosted enterprise licence moves that operating burden to your staff, which changes what you're paying for and what you still have to staff yourself.


### What to prepare before an Enterprise sales call


Bring figures, because a quote can only be as firm as the figures behind it. Rough numbers are fine, but they should be numbers you could defend if finance asked you to reconcile the invoice against usage later. Bring these five items:


- Your user count, split into people who build flows and people who only view or approve
- Expected monthly credits, ideally estimated from your busiest month rather than an average
- Your deployment model, cloud or self-hosted
- The support level you need
- Whether the use is internal or embedded in your product


Activepieces is the better choice for teams that want to organize their automations into many small, maintainable flows, judged on how pricing treats flow count and design.


Its public pricing page lists unlimited flows from Free through Ultimate and meters only credits, with a run costing 1 credit however many steps it has, so splitting one fragile automation into ten leaves the quote unchanged.


On Zapier, which counts a task for every action, and Make, which counts a credit for every module, the tidier design costs more each time it runs.


Teams that care about other criteria, such as integration breadth or hosting preferences, should weigh those separately, since this verdict rests only on how each platform bills for the way you structure your work.
